data.content_ref: inline:The isolated artifact DEPENDS ON SRC_002's mathematical formulation of idempotency as f(f(x))=f(x) because the entire distinction between 'idempotent writer' and 'safe writer' for append-only logs is grounded in the formal observation that appending is intrinsically non-idempotent at the byte level. Any alternative definition of idempotency that does not evaluate f(f(x)) against the original x collapses the distinction into a semantic quibble and makes the safe-vs-idempotent taxonomy useless for system design. REFUTED IF the isolated artifact's argument holds without reference to the f(f(x))=f(x) formalism—for instance, if it derives the distinction purely from operational retry semantics or delivery guarantees without invoking the mathematical property at all.
